editorial:
Imagine a world where time and space do not work the way they should. You get introduced to a brother and sister who have a very strange bond. One of them is obsessed with starting fires, while the other spends all their time trying to put them out. It feels like a constant game of cat and mouse, but with a deep emotional twist. The vibe is moody and a bit mysterious, making you wonder why they are stuck in this loop and what they are actually trying to achieve through these fires.

What really works here is how the movie shows their bond without needing a lot of dialogue. The acting is solid, and the visuals of the flames look great. While the slow pace might bore some people, it adds to the dreamlike feeling of the story. If you enjoy art house films that make you think, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go if you want to see every detail of the fire effects in high quality.
endingExplained: The ending reveals that the fires are not just random acts but a way for the siblings to communicate across different timelines. The brother's need to burn things and the sister's need to stop them represents their struggle to let go of the past. In the final scenes, they finally find a balance, allowing them to break the cycle. They accept their shared trauma, and the loop finally closes, giving them a sense of peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves artistic stories and family dramas.
